questions.q: Why does a country need a Constitution?
answer: A Constitution is the fundamental, supreme law of a country, and it is needed for several important reasons.

answer.text: It lays down the structure and powers of the government and the way it is to be run, so that everyone knows how decisions are made and by whom.
It guarantees the rights of citizens and states their duties, protecting people — especially minorities — from injustice.
It sets limits on the powers of the government so that no ruler or majority can become tyrannical.
It expresses the ideals and aspirations of the people, such as justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, giving the nation a common foundation.

questions.q: Describe the key features of the Indian Constitution.
answer: The Indian Constitution, framed by the Constituent Assembly and in force from 26 January 1950, has several key features.

answer.text: Government exists at more than one level — Union, State and local — each with its own powers.
The people elect their representatives through universal adult franchise, and the government is answerable to them.
Power is divided among three organs — the legislature, the executive and the judiciary — which check one another.
Fundamental Rights protect citizens against the misuse of state power, and secularism ensures the state has no official religion and treats all faiths equally.

questions.q: What does the Preamble to the Indian Constitution declare, and why is it important?

answer.text: is the introduction to the Constitution and states the ideals on which the Indian republic is built.

list: It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic
It promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens
It affirms the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation
